Semiconductor manufacturer Vishay Intertechnology ( NYSE: VSH ) fell short of the market’s revenue expectations in Q2 CY2026, but sales rose 16.6% year on year to $888.6 million. On the other hand, next quarter’s outlook exceeded expectations with revenue guided to $960 million at the midpoint, or 2% above analysts’ estimates. Its non-GAAP profit of $0.19 per share was 34.2% above analysts’ consensus estimates. Is now the time to buy Vishay Intertechnology? Find out by accessing our full research report, it’s free . Vishay Intertechnology (VSH) Q2 CY2026 Highlights: Revenue: $888.6 million vs analyst estimates of $904.9 million (16.6% year-on-year growth, 1.8% miss) Adjusted EPS: $0.19 vs analyst estimates of $0.14 (34.2% beat) Adjusted EBITDA: $104.8 million vs analyst estimates of $99.74 million (11.8% margin, 5% beat) Revenue Guidance for Q3 CY2026 is $960 million at the midpoint, above analyst estimates of $941.6 million Operating Margin: 6%, up from 2.9% in the same quarter last year Free Cash Flow was $10.31 million, up from -$73.17 million in the same quarter last year Inventory Days Outstanding: 108, in line with the previous quarter Market Capitalization: $5.96 billion “For the second quarter, Vishay delivered 9.5% sequential growth to adjusted revenue of $919 million, exceeding the top end of our revenue guidance and representing continued strengthening demand across all end markets, channels and regions,” said Joel Smejkel, president and CEO. Company Overview Named after the founder's ancestral village in present-day Lithuania, Vishay Intertechnology ( NYSE: VSH ) manufactures simple chips and electronic components that are building blocks of virtually all types of electronic devices. Revenue Growth A company’s long-term sales performance can indicate its overall quality. Even a bad business can shine for one or two quarters, but a top-tier one grows for years. Over the last five years, Vishay Intertechnology grew its sales at a mediocre 2.8% compounded annual growth rate. This was below our standards and is a rough starting point for our analysis. Semiconductors are a cyclical industry, and long-term investors should be prepared for periods of high growth followed by periods of revenue contractions. Long-term growth is the most important, but short-term results matter for semiconductors because the rapid pace of technological innovation (Moore’s Law) could make yesterday’s hit product obsolete today. Vishay Intertechnology’s annualized revenue growth of 3% over the last two years aligns with its five-year trend, suggesting its demand was consistently weak. This quarter, Vishay Intertechnology’s revenue grew by 16.6% year on year to $888.6 million but fell short of Wall Street’s estimates. Beyond the miss, this marks 5 straight quarters of growth, implying that Vishay Intertechnology is in the middle of its cycle - a typical upcycle generally lasts 8-10 quarters. Company management is currently guiding for a 21.4% year-on-year increase in sales next quarter. Looking further ahead, sell-side analysts expect revenue to grow 18.1% over the next 12 months. Product Demand & Outstanding Inventory Days Inventory Outstanding (DIO) is an important metric for chipmakers, as it reflects a business’s capital intensity and the cyclical nature of semiconductor supply and demand. In a tight supply environment, inventories tend to be stable, allowing chipmakers to exert pricing power. Steadily increasing DIO can be a warning sign that demand is weak, and if inventories continue to rise, the company may have to downsize production. This quarter, Vishay Intertechnology’s DIO came in at 108, which is 7 days above its five-year average. These numbers suggest that despite the recent decrease, the company’s inventory levels are higher than what we’ve seen in the past. Key Takeaways from Vishay Intertechnology’s Q2 Results It was good to see Vishay Intertechnology beat analysts’ EPS expectations this quarter. We were also excited its operating income outperformed Wall Street’s estimates by a wide margin. On the other hand, its revenue missed. Overall, this print was mixed. The market seemed to be hoping for more, and the stock traded down 3.5% to $37.51 immediately after reporting. Is Vishay Intertechnology an attractive investment opportunity right now? We think that the latest quarter is only one piece of the longer-term business quality puzzle. Quality, when combined with valuation, can help determine if the stock is a buy. LUMINISCENCE at St. Patrick’s Cathedral: A Light Show to Save the Church’s Historic Pipe Organ Narrated by Jonathan Roumie, Archbishop Hicks expressed enthusiasm for the project that hopes to help preserve the cathedral’s impressive organ. This month, St. Patrick’s will be illuminated via 360-degree video mapping, while guests are immersed by a blend of live choir and the LUMINISCENCE Orchestra, and the voice talent of Jonathan Roumie, who will share the story and impact of St. Patrick’s Cathedral on the community. (Photo: LUMINISCENCE/Banijay Americas) Alyssa Murphy Blogs October 4, 2026 Stepping through the massive bronze doors of St. Patrick’s Cathedral has long offered the Catholic faithful, New Yorkers and visitors alike, a sanctuary of quiet reverence. Rising majestically above Fifth Avenue, the 19th-century Neo-Gothic landmark — with its intricate white marble, soaring vaulted ceilings, and twin spires reaching more than 330 feet — stands as a sacred testament to faith, heritage and architectural splendor. Now, “America’s Parish Church” is preparing to illuminate that majesty like never before, while simultaneously supporting a vital effort to preserve its historic musical voice. The global immersive phenomenon LUMINISCENCE is debuting its latest site-specific installation inside the sacred space, pairing cutting-edge 360-degree video projection mapping with symphonic sound. Crucially, the experience serves a higher mission: A portion of ticket proceeds will directly benefit “ Renew the Living Voices: The Kilgen Organ Campaign ,” providing essential funding to restore the cathedral’s famous, aging pipe organs. The traveling show has already toured major cities in Europe and across the United States including Sacramento, Calif. “When we launched in France several years ago, we learned that each cathedral had unique challenges and ongoing needs,” explained producer Clayton Ferguson to the Register. “We found a solution that allowed the churches to address ongoing financial needs while introducing thousands of people to the beauty of their spaces.” Pastoral Support Archbishop Ronald Hicks of the Archdiocese of New York expressed enthusiasm for the project. In a statement about the program, the prelate said: “Saint Patrick’s Cathedral is truly ‘America’s Parish Church’ and one of the best known and well-loved Catholic Churches in the world. At the same time, it uniquely belongs to every New Yorker who has ever come here to pray, celebrate, find a moment of peace, or simply to marvel at its beauty.” “We are grateful for partners like LUMINISCENCE who share our commitment to caring for this historic space and inviting new generations to encounter it, be uplifted, and give glory to God — including the organ that has filled this Cathedral with music for nearly a century and that we are committed to preserving for a century more,” Archbishop Hicks added. Colorful lights grace a cathedral in Paris. (Photo: Mikhail Sytenkov) Mikhail Sytenkov Because St. Patrick’s is an active house of worship and a cherished historic landmark, adapting the show required an exceptionally reverent and collaborative approach. “We were somewhat lucky to have team members at LUMINISCENCE who had previously worked at St. Patrick’s and had even written several publications,” Ferguson noted. Drawing on these deep ties, the team presented initial storyboards to Father Enrique Salvo, rector of St. Patrick’s Cathedral. “We are eager to welcome guests to see LUMINISCENCE, experience the presence of God and embrace the beauty of light, sacred music and the remarkable story of the spiritual legacy of the Cathedral. We want all to feel at home and welcome in our Church for this experience,” Father Salvo said in a statement about the project. Father Salvo became an essential partner in refining the narrative, ensuring the installation honored the sacred dignity of the nave while carrying the full blessing of church leadership, including Archbishop Hicks and Cardinal Timothy Dolan. The light show is currently in New York City's St. Patrick's Cathedral. Anchored by a Reverent Voice To anchor the story, organizers sought a narrator who not only had professional expertise but also a strong Catholic faith. Following a top recommendation from Father Salvo, the production cast actor Jonathan Roumie, best known for portraying Jesus in The Chosen . Before his breakout role, Roumie was an established voice-over artist. During the recording sessions, his approach reflected the sacred setting. “When we were in the recording studio, Jonathan went to extraordinary efforts to ensure each line was delivered with conviction,” Ferguson shared. “He took extended moments of prayer before each section, and the results were quite moving.” Catholic actor Jonathan Roumie records his voice for the upcoming Manhattan show. (Photo: Keoni Keur/BTS Luminiscence) 2026 Keoni Keur, all rights reserved. Discreet Engineering in a Historic Sanctuary Mapping visuals across marble arches “at the millimeter” — as co-creator Romain Sarfati described — presented strict logistical rules, as nothing could harm the historic structure or interrupt daily Masses. The company uses: Concealed Rigging: The vast majority of the projection technology is completely hidden out of sight high up in the triforium balconies. Non-Invasive Mounting: Supplemental lighting uses specialized non-drilling clamps attached to marble columns, leaving no permanent marks on the stone. Optical Scale: “The absence of light tends to trick the eye, making the scale seem far larger than it actually is,” Ferguson noted, creating the illusion of looking directly into the heavens. Preserving Sacred Art and Heritage Visitors can choose from three performance tiers: “Live Plus” (full live choir and orchestra), “Live” (choir only), and “Standard LUMINISCENCE” (recorded orchestral arrangements from Budapest). Regardless of the format, every guest contributes to ensuring the cathedral’s majestic Kilgen organs continue to sound for generations to come. The massive organs date back to the early 1900s, with the dedication taking place in 1928. The largest of these instruments — the Gallery Organ — is home to more than 7,500 pipes. Since its dedication, it has been played an average of 60 hours each week, 365 days a year, filling the cathedral with approximately 300,000 hours of music. Catholic faithful attend the light show in Minneapolis. (Photo: Michael P. Bowman) MICHAEL P BOWMAN “We live in an era of competing distractions ... and we find ourselves looking down far too often,” Ferguson said. “LUMINISCENCE is an invitation to look up, and around, at the beauty and the majesty around us that we often miss.” Serious 3-D mapping of the entire cathedral is first employed to cover the entire interior canvas. The installation is currently in New York's St. Patrick's Cathedral.
